coupling: The first edited commit changes the 'seen' table allocation from stringList.size() to mapping.size(). That is benign and equivalent at that commit because mapping is still preallocated with one entry per string-list entry. The second edited commit compacts mapping so it contains only unique RLE-discovered entries and correctly updates the later string-index check to mapping.size(); with the original 'seen' allocation, that second commit remains safe. In composition, seen is sized from the now-empty/compact mapping but is still indexed by the original string index inside the RLE loop. A public IDManifest byte constructor with one valid string-index range therefore reads seen[0] from an empty vector and aborts under ASan. A correct repair must reconcile the two index domains: seen tracks original string indices and must remain sized by stringList.size(), while mapping tracks compact rank-to-original-index mappings and must use its own size for rank validation. The defect is therefore spread across the allocation change and the later representation change; each isolated commit was execution-tested clean with the same probe.
